_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Seychelles covering uninhabited period, French settlement, British colony, spice trade, independence 1976, René coup and socialism, democratic transition, ocean conservation, and tourism economy.

ethnic_groups.name: Seychellois Creole
ethnic_groups.notes: Mixed African, European (French/British), Indian, Chinese, and Malagasy descent; Creole (Kreol Seselwa) language; Catholic; no indigenous population

ethnic_groups.name: French descent
ethnic_groups.notes: Grand Blancs and Petits Blancs; original settler families; historically plantation-owning elite

ethnic_groups.name: Indian descent
ethnic_groups.notes: Gujarati, Tamil communities; arrived 19th–20th century; commerce and trade

country_profile.notes_unique: Smallest African nation by population; highest GDP per capita in Africa; 115 islands; Aldabra Atoll UNESCO site; coco de mer palm

natural_resources.notes: Exclusive Economic Zone of 1.37 million km² (vast ocean resources); Indian Ocean tuna fishing hub (Port Victoria is major tuna transhipment port); eco-tourism primary revenue source; coco de mer endemic palm; Blue Economy focus.

military.notes: Seychelles People's Defence Forces; Coast Guard primary capability; anti-piracy operations (Indian Ocean); Indian naval station (Assumption Island debated); maritime domain awareness critical.

infrastructure.notes: Cable & Wireless (Airtel); high connectivity; small but modern infrastructure.

debt_aid.notes: Highest GDP per capita in Africa; high-income economy; Blue Bond pioneer (world's first sovereign blue bond, $15M, 2018); debt restructuring 2009 (post financial crisis); tourism ~30% GDP; innovative debt-for-nature swaps.

education.notes: Free compulsory education; one of Africa's highest literacy rates; most students go abroad for university (UK, Australia, Mauritius); Creole, English, and French all used in education; small scale limits specialisation.

diaspora_migration.notes: Small population means diaspora proportionally significant; foreign workers (~15% of workforce) from India, Bangladesh, Philippines, Madagascar for construction and services; brain drain concern.
diaspora_migration.immigration_policy: Work permits for tourism/construction; migrant labor (India, Bangladesh)

digital_economy.notes: SEAS submarine cable (2012) transformed connectivity; Cable & Wireless (Airtel) and Intelvision operators; high mobile penetration (nearly 200%); Blue Economy digital initiatives; e-government services advancing.

country_profile.national_motto: Finis Coronat Opus (The End Crowns the Work)

geography.terrain: 115 islands: 41 granitic (inner, mountainous) + 74 coralline (outer, flat atolls); tropical rainforest; white sand beaches; coral reefs
geography.notes: Smallest African country by population (~100k); 115 islands; only granitic oceanic islands worldwide; Vallée de Mai (coco de mer palms, UNESCO); Aldabra Atoll (UNESCO, largest raised coral atoll); highest GDP per capita in Africa.

economy_extended.notes: Highest GDP per capita in Africa; tourism-dependent (60%+ GDP); tuna fishing/canning (Indian Ocean Tuna Ltd); offshore financial center; blue economy strategy.

health.notes: Free universal healthcare; best health indicators in Africa; heroin epidemic challenge; non-communicable diseases dominate; small hospital system.

food_agriculture.notes: 90% food imported; tuna fishing major industry; cinnamon and vanilla exports; limited arable land; aquaculture developing; food price vulnerability.

energy.notes: PUC (Public Utilities Corporation); diesel/heavy fuel dependent; target 15% renewables by 2030; floating solar pilot; wind turbines on Mahé.

transport.notes: Inter-island ferries (Cat Cocos/Cat Rose); small road network; helicopter transfers; Praslin-La Digue ferry.

major_attractions: Anse Source d'Argent (La Digue, most photographed beach)
Vallée de Mai (coco de mer, prehistoric palms)
tourism.notes: Best passport in Africa; luxury eco-tourism; honeymooner paradise; coco de mer unique; Aldabra giant tortoises; sustainability focus; seabird colonies.

human_rights_gender.notes: Multi-party democracy since 1993; 2020 first opposition victory; progressive social policies; drug trafficking concern; matrilineal culture historically.

border_disputes: Chagos Archipelago (supports Mauritius claim vs UK)
security_stability.notes: One of most peaceful globally; piracy concern (Somali waters proximity); drug trafficking route; small military (SPDF—300 personnel).

cultural_heritage.national_dish: Grilled fish with Creole sauce and rice
cultural_heritage.media_landscape: SBC state; Le Seychellois Hebdo; Nation newspaper; small but diverse media
cultural_heritage.notes: Creole culture (African+European+Asian fusion); coco de mer (largest seed in world); giant tortoises; Festival Kreol; matrilineal influences.

legal_system.legal_tradition: Hybrid: English common law (criminal) and French civil law (property, civil)
legal_system.notes: Supreme Court and Court of Appeal; Anti-piracy courts (regional jurisdiction under UNODC); small but effective legal system.

comparative_rankings.notes: #1 HDI, GDP per capita, and life expectancy in Africa.

former_leaders.name: James Mancham
former_leaders.notes: First president; SDP; pro-Western; overthrown by René's coup while at Commonwealth summit

former_leaders.name: France-Albert René
former_leaders.notes: SPPF; socialist one-party state 1977–1993; survived multiple coup attempts; transitioned to multiparty 1993; retired voluntarily

former_leaders.name: James Michel
former_leaders.notes: SPPF/PL; René's ally; Blue Economy advocate; resigned

former_leaders.name: Danny Faure
former_leaders.notes: PL; completed Michel's term; lost to Ramkalawan 2020
